models.summary: Undisturbed forest carbon follows a logistic rate, r times stock times 1 minus stock over the maximum. Felled carbon is a cutting intensity times the stock. Stability sets the rate equal to the felled stock and requires the intensity below the growth rate. The fastest point is half the maximum, so the printed optimum is the growth rate over 2. This year is last year plus the rate minus the cut. After planting, the same symbol is written on both sides. Product carbon is a production discount times last year felled carbon plus last year products. The system stock adds the forest to the products.
models.computational_cost: One logistic step per year plus one product accumulation
models.purpose: Turn a growth rate and a cutting intensity into a forest-plus-product stock.
objectives: Maximize system carbon while keeping the intensity at half the inherent growth rate.

models.summary: Three objectives: minimize the gap between production and demand for fuel-like and furniture-like products, maximize profit minus planting cost, and maximize forest stock plus product stock. The recurrence writes this year stock inside the logistic term. Product carbon splits into a fuel part and a durable part, and only the durable part survives at rate 1 minus beta. The cut over the stock stays below the primed growth rate. Planting cost is a unit cost times the cut over mature density, with an extra factor on the line. Production is storage volume times product carbon over density. Profit must not go negative, and production stays between half and one and a half times demand. A genetic algorithm treats the two cut volumes as genes.
models.computational_cost: A genetic search over two annual product volumes
